answer: Submissions that land within 255 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The horizon detector writes to haven, and vine shows every merge. A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 193 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 19 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
